newsitem.title: CROATIA: Still no date for Croatia pipeline sale to MOL.
newsitem.headline: Still no date for Croatia pipeline sale to MOL.

text.p: Croatian privatisation authorities said on Wednesday there was no definite date yet for the sale of an Adriatic pipeline stake to Hungary's MOL which was formally approved three months ago.
"There are some details that still have to be polished," spokesman for the Croatian privatisation agency (HFP) Neven Andrilovic told Reuters.
MOL had offered to pay some 90 million German marks ($52.2 million) for a 12.5-percent stake in the pipeline operator Janaf at last year's tender.
Although its bid was accepted by HFP's board in January, the sale never came to fruition. Some local media recently blamed restructuring within MOL for the delay.
Hungarian partners last visited Zagreb earlier in April to discuss the deal with top officials. But the two sides agreed not to reveal anything before it was struck, Andrilovic said.
Between 30 and 40 percent of the pipeline, which links the Adriatic with central Europe, is due for an international offering later this year via Detsche Morgan Grenfell.

It currently operates at no more than 10-15 percent of the total annual capacity, 3.5 million tonnes of crude a year. It now has only one big user, the state oil firm INA Industrija Nafte, which controls 33 percent of Janaf.
The pipeline is thought to be a good alternative route for crude shipments to Russia's Druzhba pipeline. Industry analysts believe its capacity could easily be expanded with very minor investments.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) has been mentioned among the parties interested in Janaf's selloff and restructuring.
The company's shares last week fetched 6,400 kuna on Zagreb's bourse but traded volume was rather small.
-- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075 ($ = 1.724 German Marks)
